research_question: Does target-independent inverse-frequency weighting improve a randomized tree ensemble under fresh leave-one-element-out band-gap shifts, while retaining the v2 Extra Trees advantage over GPU CatBoost?
hypothesis: The training distribution overweights common elemental environments. Stoichiometric inverse-frequency row weighting will make randomized tree partitions less dominated by common elements and lower element-macro MAE on unseen-element shifts.
falsifier: Development does not justify protected confirmation unless a nonzero frequency exponent improves macro MAE over its aggregation-matched unweighted Extra Trees control by more than 0.01 eV, improves at least five of eight fresh elements, improves over the CatBoost ensemble by more than 0.02 eV, and produces complete finite evidence.
novelty_boundary: Extra Trees, inverse-frequency weighting, and ensemble aggregation are individually established. The testable contribution is their target-independent composition-frequency weighting rule and its preregistered evaluation under element exclusion; no claim of a new tree algorithm is made.
development_panel_rule: Chosen before v3 outcomes from target-independent full-dataset occurrence counts. The panel spans common and sparse elements, anions, metalloids, post-transition metals, an alkaline-earth metal, and a transition metal. It excludes all v1/v2 outer development elements, all v2 pseudo-exclusion elements, and all protected elements.

representation.name: v1 fractions and periodic moments plus Magpie ElementProperty and Stoichiometry

frequency_balance.formula: Normalize sum_e fraction(i,e) * (training_occurrence(e)/n_train)^(-alpha), clip to [0.25,4.0], renormalize to mean one

selection_rule: Select the nonzero-exponent candidate with minimum element-macro MAE across the eight development elements. Candidates within 0.003 eV of the minimum choose the smaller exponent, then mean aggregation before median.
primary_metric: element-macro mean absolute error in eV
secondary_metrics: sample-weight range and effective sample size
independent_units: eight element-exclusion scenarios; overlapping rows are retained and must be clustered by row identity in any bootstrap analysis
